  • Concepts used: Verb tense agreement and prepositions/conjunctions of concession.

Solution

  • Blank 1: The sentence discusses a completed action in the past ("more than 300 runs in 20 overs"). The appropriate verb form is the past tense "scored".
  • Blank 2: The sentence contrasts the high score with the presence of "rains". The correct preposition to show this contrast (in spite of) is "despite". Note that "despite" is never followed by "of", whereas "in spite" must be followed by "of".

questions.question:
If a positive real \( x \) satisfies the following equation
\[\log_2 x + \log_{\sqrt{2}} x = 48, \]
then the value of \( x \) is ________________
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Numerical Computation and Estimation

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given: The logarithmic equation \(\log_{2}x + \log_{\sqrt{2}}x = 48\).
  • Find: The value of positive real \(x\).
  • Concepts used: Logarithm base change properties.

Solution

  • Apply the base power rule of logarithms: \(\log_{b^k}x = \dfrac{1}{k}\log_{b}x\).
  • The base of the second term is \(\sqrt{2} = 2^{0.5}\). Therefore:\[\log_{\sqrt{2}}x = \dfrac{1}{0.5}\log_{2}x = 2\log_{2}x\]
  • Substitute back into the original equation:\[\log_{2}x + 2\log_{2}x = 48\]\[3\log_{2}x = 48\]\[\log_{2}x = 16\]
  • Convert to exponential form:\[x = 2^{16}\]

Final Answer

Answer: \(2^{16}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

  • Find: The statement that is necessarily true based on this falsehood.

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | GA Q5
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about four numbers:
(S1) The average of the four numbers is 25
(S2) Each number is at most 40
(S3) Each number is at least 20
Choose the option that is necessarily correct.
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Numerical Relations and Reasoning

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given: Four numbers with three conditional statements:
    • (S1) Average is 25
    • (S2) Each number is \(\le 40\)
    • (S3) Each number is \(\ge 20\)
  • Find: The logically necessary relationship between the statements.
  • Concepts used: Averages, maximum/minimum bounding.

Solution

  • Let the four numbers be \(a, b, c, d\). From (S1), their sum \(= 25 \times 4 = 100\).
  • Testing whether (S1) and (S3) together imply (S2):
    • Assume (S1) and (S3) are true: sum \(= 100\), and each number \(\ge 20\).
    • To maximize one number (say \(a\)), minimize the other three at their lower bound of 20 each.
    • Maximum possible value of \(a = 100 - (20 + 20 + 20) = 40\).
    • Since the maximum possible value for any number is 40, each number must be \(\le 40\) — this is exactly statement (S2).
  • Thus, (S1) and (S3) together force (S2) to be true.

Final Answer

Answer: (S1) and (S3) together imply (S2).  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.question: Consider a string P of length \( l \) that is laid out as a straight-line segment. Another string K is laid out as a semicircular arc with string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (i). When both the strings are shortened by a length \( x \) they can be re-arranged such that the shortened string K forms a full circle with the shortened string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (ii). The value of \( x/l \) is
questions.explanation:
Quantitative Aptitude → Mensuration and Geometry

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given:
    • String P has length \(l\).
    • String K is a semicircle with diameter \(l\).
    • Both strings are shortened by \(x\).
    • Shortened K forms a full circle with shortened P as its diameter.
  • Find: The ratio \(x/l\).
  • Concepts used: Circumference of circles and semicircles.

Solution

  • Initial state: Radius of semicircular arc K \(= l/2\). Its arc length:\[L_K = \pi \times \dfrac{l}{2} = \dfrac{\pi l}{2}\]
  • Shortened state:
    • Length of shortened P \(= l - x\) → this is the diameter of the new circle.
    • Length of shortened K \(= \dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x\) → this is the circumference of the new circle.
  • Equate and solve (circumference \(= \pi \times\) diameter):\[\dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi(l - x)\]\[\dfrac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi l - \pi x\]\[\pi x - x = \pi l - \dfrac{\pi l}{2}\]\[x(\pi - 1) = \dfrac{\pi l}{2}\]\[\dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi - 1)}\]

Final Answer

Answer: \(\dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi - 1)}\)  |  Correct option: (C)

The Roman senator Meritorius, his brother, his son, and his daughter have varying oratory skill levels. They are seated in rows and columns as shown in the figure with exactly one person sitting in each box. It is known that
(i) Meritorius' daughter and his brother are seated in the same column.
(ii) His son is seated diagonally across the sibling of the worst orator.
(iii) The best and worst orators are seated in the same row.

Who is the best orator?

Seating Arrangement
questions.explanation:
Analytical Aptitude → Logic

Problem Analysis

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given: 4 people (Meritorius, Brother, Son, Daughter) in a 2×2 grid with constraints:
    1. Daughter and Brother are in the same column.
    2. Son is diagonally across the sibling of the worst orator.
    3. Best and worst orators are in the same row.
  • Find: The identity of the best orator.
  • Concepts used: Matrix logic puzzles, constraint satisfaction.

Solution

  • From constraint (i): Daughter (D) and Brother (B) occupy one column; Meritorius (M) and Son (S) occupy the other column.
  • From constraint (ii): Son is diagonally across the "sibling of the worst orator". For a diagonal relationship, this sibling must be in the other column, i.e., either D or B.
    • Case 1 — Sibling is D: Worst orator = S (since D and S are siblings). By constraint (iii), best orator shares a row with S → that person is B. Best orator = B.
    • Case 2 — Sibling is B: Worst orator = M (since B and M are siblings). By constraint (iii), best orator shares a row with M → that person is B. Best orator = B.
  • In all valid logical frameworks, the best orator is Meritorius' brother.

Final Answer

Answer: Meritorius' brother  |  Correct option: (B)

Trace of a Matrix: The trace of any square matrix is fundamentally equal to the sum of its eigenvalues.\[\text{Trace}(A) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \lambda_i \]

    • \(\lambda_2^2 = 2^2 = 4\)
    • \(\lambda_3^2 = 3^2 = 9\)

    \[\text{Trace}(A^2) = \lambda_1^2 + \lambda_2^2 + \lambda_3^2 \]\[\text{Trace}(A^2) = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14 | Correct option: (B)

questions.question:
A fifth-degree polynomial in \( x \) is defined for \( x > 0 \). All coefficients of the polynomial are positive. The first derivative of the polynomial is obtained numerically at a point by using the first-order forward as well as the first-order backward difference methods. Identical step lengths are used for both the methods.

Following statements are made.
(I) Forward difference method underestimates the true derivative.
(II) Backward difference method overestimates the true derivative.

Which one of the following options is CORRECT?
options: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.
Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.
structuredOptions.html: Statement (I) is TRUE and statement (II) is FALSE.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.
structuredOptions.html: Statement (I) is FALSE and statement (II) is TRUE.

questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Numerical Methods

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • \(P(x)\): 5th-degree polynomial for \(x > 0\).
    • All coefficients are strictly positive (\(a_i > 0\)).
    • Derivatives obtained numerically via first-order forward and backward difference methods.
  • Aim: Evaluate validity of Statements (I) and (II) regarding whether these methods under/overestimate the true first derivative.

3. Core Concepts:

Function behavior: For \(P(x) = a_5x^5 + a_4x^4 + a_3x^3 + a_2x^2 + a_1x + a_0\) with all \(a_i > 0\) and \(x > 0\), the second derivative \(P''(x)\) is strictly positive. A positive second derivative means the function is strictly convex (concave upward).

Taylor Series Expansion:
Forward Step: \(f(x+h) = f(x) + hf'(x) + \dfrac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_1)\)
Backward Step: \(f(x-h) = f(x) - hf'(x) + \dfrac{h^2}{2}f''(\xi_2)\)

4. Solution Method:

By manipulating the Taylor expansions, we can find expressions for the numerical derivatives and compare them directly to the exact analytical derivative \(f'(x)\). The sign of the truncation error (which depends on \(f''(x)\)) dictates whether it's an overestimate or underestimate.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Evaluate Forward Difference Method:
    From Taylor series:\[\dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = f'(x) + \dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_1) \]Since \(f''(x) > 0\) for all \(x > 0\), the error term \(\dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_1)\) is positive.
    Therefore, Forward Difference value \(>\) True \(f'(x)\).
    Conclusion: Forward difference overestimates the true derivative. (Statement I says it underestimates → FALSE).
  2. Evaluate Backward Difference Method:
    From Taylor series:\[\dfrac{f(x) - f(x-h)}{h} = f'(x) - \dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_2) \]Since \(f''(x) > 0\), the term being subtracted \(\dfrac{h}{2}f''(\xi_2)\) is positive.
    Therefore, Backward Difference value \(<\) True \(f'(x)\).
    Conclusion: Backward difference underestimates the true derivative. (Statement II says it overestimates → FALSE).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Both statements (I) and (II) are FALSE | Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
Periodic function \( f(x) \) is given below.
\[f(x) = \begin{cases} -1, & \text{when } -\pi < x < 0 \\ 1, & \text{when } 0 < x < \pi \end{cases} ; f(x + 2\pi) = f(x) \]
The CORRECT option representing the Fourier series expansion of \( f(x) \) is:
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Calculus (Fourier Series)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(f(x) = -1\) for \(-\pi < x < 0\)
    • \(f(x) = 1\) for \(0 < x < \pi\)
    • Period \(T = 2\pi\)
  • Aim: Determine the CORRECT Fourier series expansion for \(f(x)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Symmetry (Odd/Even Functions): Since \(f(-x) = -f(x)\), the function is odd.

Fourier Coefficients for Odd Functions:

  • \(a_0 = 0\)
  • \(a_n = 0\) (No cosine terms)
  • \(b_n = \dfrac{2}{L} \int_{0}^{L} f(x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{L}\right) dx\), where \(L = \pi\) (half-period).

4. Solution Method:

Compute the \(b_n\) coefficients integrating over \(0\) to \(\pi\) where \(f(x) = 1\), and construct the sine series.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formula Setup for \(b_n\):\[b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi} (1) \cdot \sin(nx)\, dx \]
  2. Integration:\[ b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \left[\dfrac{-\cos(nx)}{n} \right]_{0}^{\pi} \]\[ b_n = \dfrac{-2}{n\pi}[\cos(n\pi) - \cos(0)] \]Recall that \(\cos(n\pi) = (-1)^n\) and \(\cos(0) = 1\).\[ b_n = \dfrac{-2}{n\pi}[(-1)^n - 1] = \dfrac{2}{n\pi}[1 - (-1)^n] \]
  3. Evaluate for Even and Odd \(n\):
    • If \(n\) is even (2, 4, 6, ...): \(1 - (1) = 0 \Rightarrow b_n = 0\)
    • If \(n\) is odd (1, 3, 5, ...): \(1 - (-1) = 2 \Rightarrow b_n = \dfrac{4}{n\pi}\)
  4. Construct the Series:\[f(x) = \sum_{n=1,3,5}^{\infty} \dfrac{4}{n\pi} \sin(nx) \]\[ f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \left[\sin x + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\sin 5x}{5} + \cdots \right] \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \left[\sin x + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \cdots \right]\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
A rectangular singly reinforced concrete beam has a width of 300 mm and an effective depth of 550 mm. The grades of steel and concrete are Fe500 and M25, respectively. The area of steel in tension is 1963 mm². The depth of neutral axis is 302 mm. The ratio of the limiting depth of the neutral axis (\(x_{u,max}\)) to the effective depth (\(d\)) of the beam is 0.456.
The most probable mode of failure of the beam is
questions.explanation:
RCC Design | Limit State Design of Beams

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Width \(b = 300\) mm
    • Effective depth \(d = 550\) mm
    • Grade of steel: Fe500, Grade of concrete: M25
    • Area of steel in tension \(A_{st} = 1963\) mm\(^2\)
    • Actual depth of neutral axis \(x_u = 302\) mm
    • Limiting depth ratio \(x_{u,max}/d = 0.456\)
  • Aim: Determine the most probable mode of failure.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 456:2000 Limits: Defines limiting neutral axis depth (\(x_{u,max}\)) to prevent sudden brittle failures.

  • Under-reinforced Section (\(x_u < x_{u,max}\)): Steel yields before concrete crushes. Leads to ductile failure with ample warning (tension failure).
  • Over-reinforced Section (\(x_u > x_{u,max}\)): Concrete reaches ultimate strain (\(\epsilon_{cu} = 0.0035\)) before steel yields. Leads to a sudden, explosive crushing of concrete (compression failure).

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the absolute value of \(x_{u,max}\) from the given ratio and compare it to the given actual neutral axis depth (\(x_u\)). The relation between these two dictates the failure mode.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Limiting Neutral Axis Depth (\(x_{u,max}\)):\[x_{u,max} = \left( \dfrac{x_{u,max}}{d} \right) \times d \]\[x_{u,max} = 0.456 \times 550 = 250.8 \text{ mm} \]
  2. Compare Actual \(x_u\) with \(x_{u,max}\):
    • Given \(x_u = 302\) mm
    • Since \(302 \text{ mm} > 250.8 \text{ mm}\), we have \(x_u > x_{u,max}\).
  3. Interpret Result:
    Because the actual neutral axis is deeper than the limiting neutral axis, the section has too much steel. It is an over-reinforced section. Such sections fail abruptly due to concrete crushing before yielding of steel occurs. This is termed a compression failure.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Compression Failure | Correct option: (A)

questions.question:
As per IS:800-2007, design of a cantilever steel beam section for its moment capacity requires fulfilment of an upper bound, expressed as:
\[M_d \le 1.5Z_e \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}} \]
The reason for such upper bound is to
options: avoid plastic deformation under working load

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: avoid plastic deformation under working load
structuredOptions.html: avoid plastic deformation under working load

questions.explanation:
Steel Structures | Design of Flexural Members

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Upper bound moment capacity limit for cantilever beam: \(M_d \le 1.5\, Z_e\, \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}\)
  • Aim: Identify the structural rationale behind this specific upper bound limit per IS 800:2007.

3. Core Concepts:

IS 800:2007 Clause 8.2.1.2: Dictates the design bending strength for laterally supported beams.

  • While section capacity relies on the plastic section modulus (\(Z_p\)), relying purely on \(Z_p\) could mean the extreme fibers yield substantially under service (working) loads, leading to permanent set/deformation.
  • The code imposes a limit based on the elastic section modulus (\(Z_e\)) multiplied by a shape factor limit (1.2 for simply supported, 1.5 for cantilevers) to restrict extreme fiber yielding at service load limits.

4. Solution Method:

Direct theoretical recall of IS Code philosophy. The clause strictly enforces this limit to ensure elastic behavior under serviceability limit states.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • \(Z_e f_y / \gamma_{m0}\) represents the elastic moment capacity (first yield).
  • If bending moments are allowed to vastly exceed this (approaching full plastic moment \(Z_p f_y\)), the beam fibers will undergo plastic strains. When the load is removed, the beam will not return to its original geometry.
  • The literal text of IS 800:2007 Clause 8.2.1.2 explicitly states: “...to avoid plastic deformation under working loads, \(M_d\) shall be less than or equal to \(1.2\, Z_e f_y / \gamma_{m0}\) in case of simply supported beams and \(1.5\, Z_e f_y / \gamma_{m0}\) in case of cantilever beams.”

6. Final Answer:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: A body subjected to plane strain conditions in the X-Y plane.
  • Aim: Identify the correct strain constraints that define this condition mathematically.

3. Core Concepts:

Plane Strain: A state of strain where the dimension of the body in one direction (usually the Z-direction) is very large compared to the other two, or is rigidly constrained. Because it cannot deform in the Z-direction, all strain components associated with the Z-axis are strictly zero.

  • Normal strain \(\epsilon_{zz} = 0\)
  • Out-of-plane shear strains \(\gamma_{xz} = 0\), \(\gamma_{yz} = 0\) (i.e., \(\epsilon_{xz} = \epsilon_{yz} = 0\))

Note: While strains in Z are zero, the stress in Z (\(\sigma_{zz}\)) is not zero due to the Poisson effect: \(\sigma_{zz} = \nu(\sigma_{xx} + \sigma_{yy})\).

4. Solution Method:

Check the options against the fundamental definition:

  • Option (A): \(\sigma_{zz} = 0\) corresponds to Plane Stress.
  • Option (B): \(\epsilon_{zz} = \epsilon_{xz} = \epsilon_{yz} = 0\) perfectly matches the Plane Strain definition.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

By the theoretical definition of X-Y Plane Strain, no deformations occur along the Z-axis or relative to the Z-axis:

\[\epsilon_{zz} = \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial z} = 0 \]\[\gamma_{xz} = \dfrac{\partial u}{\partial z} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial x} = 0 \implies \epsilon_{xz} = 0 \]\[\gamma_{yz} = \dfrac{\partial v}{\partial z} + \dfrac{\partial w}{\partial y} = 0 \implies \epsilon_{yz} = 0 \]

Hence, \(\epsilon_{zz} = \epsilon_{xz} = \epsilon_{yz} = 0\).

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\epsilon_{zz} = \epsilon_{xz} = \epsilon_{yz} = 0\) | Correct option: (B)

3. Core Concepts:

Pure Shear Definition: A stress state where there are mutually perpendicular planes entirely devoid of normal stresses, experiencing only shear stress (\(\tau\)).

Mohr's Circle: For pure shear, the Mohr's circle is centered exactly at the origin \((0, 0)\).

Principal Stresses of Pure Shear: If you rotate a pure shear element by \(45^\circ\), the resulting principal planes will have normal stresses equal in magnitude but opposite in sign (\(\sigma_1 = \tau\), \(\sigma_2 = -\tau\)), and zero shear stress. Thus, the condition for pure shear along principal axes is \(\sigma_x + \sigma_y = 0\) (volumetric/hydrostatic stress is zero).

4. Solution Method:

Analyze the orthogonal normal stress vectors (\(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_y\)) in each option, ensuring standard sign conventions (Tension = Positive, Compression = Negative). Calculate the average stress \((\sigma_x + \sigma_y)/2\). If it equals 0, it represents pure shear.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Option\(\sigma_x\) (MPa)\(\sigma_y\) (MPa)\(\sigma_{avg}\)State
(A)+40 (Tension)−40 (Compression)0Pure Shear ✔
(B)+40 (Tension)+40 (Tension)+40Biaxial Tension
(C)−40 (Compression)−40 (Compression)−40Biaxial Compression
(D)+40 (Tension)0+20Uniaxial Tension

Option (A) Analysis:
Horizontal faces (Left/Right): Arrows point away from the block → Tension, \(\sigma_x = +40\) MPa.
Vertical faces (Top/Bottom): Arrows point towards the block → Compression, \(\sigma_y = -40\) MPa.
Center of Mohr's Circle: \(\sigma_{avg} = (+40 - 40)/2 = 0\). → Represents a pure shear state (with max shear magnitude \(\tau_{max} = 40\) MPa on planes oriented \(45^\circ\) to the axes).

6. Final Answer:

    • Loading: UDL of \(5\text{ kN/m}\) on F-G, point load \(20\text{ kN}\) at G, point load \(30\text{ kN}\) at H, UDL of \(4\text{ kN/m}\) on K-L.
  • Aim: Calculate the upward vertical reaction at the fixed support L (\(V_L\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Internal Hinges: An internal hinge cannot transmit bending moment (\(M = 0\)). It transfers only shear force and axial force.
  • Beam Decomposition: A continuous beam with internal hinges can be broken down into stable “supporting” parts (cantilevers) and “suspended” parts (simply supported beams resting on the supporting parts).
  • Static Equilibrium: \(\sum F_y = 0\) and \(\sum M = 0\).

  1. Decompose the Beam based on the hinges:
    • Span F-G: Cantilever fixed at F, supporting hinge G.
    • Span G-J: Suspended simply supported beam resting on hinges G and J.
    • Span J-L: Cantilever fixed at L, supporting hinge J.
  2. Analyze the Suspended Span (G-J): Length \(= 2 + 2 = 4\text{ m}\). Point load \(30\text{ kN}\) acts at H (midpoint of G-J). The \(20\text{ kN}\) load acts directly at hinge G and transfers to cantilever F-G without inducing shear across G-J. By symmetry, reaction at J is half the central load.
  3. Analyze the Supporting Span (J-L): Apply equilibrium using the transferred reaction at J and the UDL on K-L.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Reaction at hinge J from suspended span G-J:
    Downward load at midpoint H \(= 30\text{ kN}\).

  2. Loads on cantilever span J-L:

    • UDL from K to L \(= 4\text{ kN/m} \times 2\text{ m} = 8\text{ kN}\) (downwards).
  3. Apply static equilibrium to find \(V_L\):\[\sum F_y = 0 \implies V_L = R_J + (\text{UDL} \times L_{KL}) \]\[V_L = 15 + 8 = 23\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 23 kN | Correct option: (A)

  • Given Data: A simply supported beam of length \(L\) and flexural rigidity \(EI\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Müller-Breslau Principle: The ILD for any stress function is given by the deflected shape when a unit displacement/rotation corresponding to that function is applied.
  • Maxwell-Betti Reciprocal Theorem: The rotation at B due to a unit load at \(x\) equals the deflection at \(x\) due to a unit moment at B.

4. Solution Method:

Apply a unit clockwise moment (\(M_B = 1\)) at B and find the elastic deflection curve \(y(x)\) using the Conjugate Beam Method.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find reactions for unit clockwise moment at B:
    \(\sum M_A = 0\): \(R_B \times L = 1 \Rightarrow R_B = \dfrac{1}{L}\) (upward).
    \(\sum F_y = 0\): \(R_A = \dfrac{1}{L}\) (downward).
  2. Bending moment at distance \(x\) from A:\[M(x) = -R_A \cdot x = -\dfrac{x}{L} \]
  3. Conjugate Beam Method:
    The conjugate beam carries a triangular \(M/EI\) load varying from \(0\) at A to \(\dfrac{1}{EIL}\) at B (downward/negative).
    Total load: \(W = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot L \cdot \dfrac{1}{EIL} = \dfrac{1}{2EI}\)
    Conjugate reaction at A (moments about B):\[R^*_A \cdot L = \dfrac{1}{2EI} \cdot \dfrac{L}{3} \implies R^*_A = \dfrac{1}{6EI} \text{ (downward)} \]
  4. Deflection (conjugate bending moment) at \(x\):\[y(x) = M^*(x) = -\dfrac{x}{6EI} + \dfrac{x^3}{6EIL} = \dfrac{1}{6EIL}\left(x^3 - L^2 x\right) \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\dfrac{1}{6EIL}\left(x^3 - L^2 x\right)\) | Correct option: (B)

questions.question:
Consider differential equation \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy = x \) with the condition as \( y = 0 \) at \( x = 0 \).
The value of \( y \) at \( x = 1.0 \) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Differential Equations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Differential Equation: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy = x\)
    • Boundary Condition: \(y = 0\) at \(x = 0\)
  • Aim: Find the value of \(y\) at \(x = 1.0\) (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • First-Order Linear ODE: Standard form: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P(x)y = Q(x)\)
  • Integrating Factor (IF): \(IF = e^{\int P(x)\,dx}\)
  • General Solution: \(y \cdot (IF) = \int Q(x) \cdot (IF)\,dx + C\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify \(P(x)\) and \(Q(x)\).
  2. Compute the Integrating Factor.
  3. Integrate to find the general solution.
  4. Apply the boundary condition to find constant \(C\).
  5. Evaluate \(y(1.0)\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Identify: \(P(x) = x\), \(Q(x) = x\)
  2. Integrating Factor:\[IF = e^{\int x\,dx} = e^{x^2/2} \]
  3. General Solution:\[y \cdot e^{x^2/2} = \int x \cdot e^{x^2/2}\,dx + C \]Let \(u = \dfrac{x^2}{2} \Rightarrow du = x\,dx\):\[y \cdot e^{x^2/2} = e^{x^2/2} + C \]Dividing by \(e^{x^2/2}\):\[y(x) = 1 + Ce^{-x^2/2} \]
  4. Apply Boundary Condition (\(y = 0\) at \(x = 0\)):\[0 = 1 + C \implies C = -1 \]Specific solution: \(y(x) = 1 - e^{-x^2/2}\)
  5. Evaluate at \(x = 1.0\):\[y(1.0) = 1 - e^{-0.5} = 1 - 0.6065 = 0.3935 \approx 0.39 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.39 | Accepted key range: 0.37 to 0.42

questions.question:
The age (in years) of a population is normally distributed with a mean of 36 and standard deviation of 12. The height (in cm) of the same population is also normally distributed with a mean of 160 and standard deviation of 10.
If the probability of age greater than 50 years is equal to the probability of height greater than \( h \), the value of \( h \) (in cm) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Engineering Mathematics | Probability & Statistics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Age distribution: \(A \sim N(\mu_A = 36,\ \sigma_A = 12)\)
    • Height distribution: \(H \sim N(\mu_H = 160,\ \sigma_H = 10)\)
    • Condition: \(P(A > 50) = P(H > h)\)
  • Aim: Find the value of height \(h\) in cm (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Standardization: Any normal variate \(X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)\) is converted to standard normal using:\[Z = \dfrac{X - \mu}{\sigma} \]
  • If \(P(A > x_1) = P(H > x_2)\), their corresponding \(Z\)-scores must be equal.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the \(Z\)-score for Age \(= 50\).
  2. Set this equal to the \(Z\)-score formula for Height \(= h\).
  3. Solve for \(h\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. \(Z\)-score for Age \(= 50\):\[Z_A = \dfrac{50 - 36}{12} = \dfrac{14}{12} = \dfrac{7}{6} \]
  2. Equate to \(Z\)-score for Height \(= h\):\[\dfrac{h - 160}{10} = \dfrac{7}{6} \]
  3. Solve for \(h\):\[h - 160 = 10 \times \dfrac{7}{6} = \dfrac{70}{6} = 11.6667 \]\[h = 160 + 11.6667 = 171.67\text{ cm} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 171.67 cm | Accepted key range: 170.00 to 173.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q48

questions.question:
A 250 mm wide × 600 mm deep rectangular concrete beam is prestressed by means of 4 high-tensile tendons, each of 14 mm diameter. The centre of the tendons is 200 mm from the soffit of the beam. The effective stress in each tendon is 700 N/mm².
The maximum bending moment (in kN-m), that can be applied to the section without causing tension at the soffit of the beam due to prestressing only, is ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
Use \( \pi = 3.14 \)
questions.explanation:
Structural Engineering | Prestressed Concrete

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Beam dimensions: \(b = 250\text{ mm}\), \(D = 600\text{ mm}\)
    • Tendons: 4 numbers, diameter \(d = 14\text{ mm}\)
    • Center of tendons is \(200\text{ mm}\) from the soffit (bottom)
    • Effective prestress: \(f_p = 700\text{ N/mm}^2\)
    • Condition: Maximum applied bending moment \(M\) without causing tension at the soffit.
    • Use \(\pi = 3.14\)
  • Aim: Find the maximum bending moment \(M\) in kN·m.

3. Core Concepts:

Stress at the bottom fiber (IS 1343):\[\sigma_{\text{bottom}} = \dfrac{P}{A} + \dfrac{P \cdot e}{Z} - \dfrac{M}{Z} \]

Zero Tension Condition: Set \(\sigma_{\text{bottom}} = 0\):\[M = P\left(\dfrac{Z}{A} + e\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate cross-sectional area (\(A\)) and section modulus (\(Z\)).
  2. Compute eccentricity (\(e\)) from the neutral axis.
  3. Calculate the prestressing force (\(P\)).
  4. Set \(\sigma_{\text{bottom}} = 0\) and solve for \(M\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Section Properties:
    • \(A = 250 \times 600 = 150{,}000\text{ mm}^2\)
    • Centroidal depth from soffit \(= D/2 = 300\text{ mm}\)
    • \(Z = \dfrac{b \cdot D^2}{6} = \dfrac{250 \times 600^2}{6} = 15 \times 10^6\text{ mm}^3\)
    • Kern distance: \(\dfrac{Z}{A} = \dfrac{15 \times 10^6}{150{,}000} = 100\text{ mm}\)
  2. Eccentricity (\(e\)):\[e = 300\text{ mm} - 200\text{ mm} = 100\text{ mm} \]
  3. Prestressing Force (\(P\)):
    Area of tendons: \(A_p = 4 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4} \times d^2 = \pi \times d^2 = 3.14 \times 196 = 615.44\text{ mm}^2\)
    \[P = A_p \times f_p = 615.44 \times 700 = 430{,}808\text{ N} \]
  4. Maximum Moment \(M\):\[M = P \left(\dfrac{Z}{A} + e\right) = 430{,}808 \times (100 + 100) = 430{,}808 \times 200 \]\[M = 86{,}161{,}600\text{ N·mm} = 86.16\text{ kN·m} \approx 86.2\text{ kN·m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 86.2 kN·m | Accepted key range: 85.50 to 87.60

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Concrete & Steel Structures
questions.topic: Steel Tension, Compression Members & Plastic Analysis
questions.question:
A rigid-jointed portal frame, shown in the figure, consists of beam and columns of equal length L. The frame has a fixed support at one end and a roller support at the other end. The frame is subjected to a uniformly distributed load w and a lateral load P as shown in the figure. The plastic moment capacity of the beam and column sections is Mp. Consider a combined beam-column mechanism for plastic collapse. By applying the virtual work equation corresponding to the combined plastic collapse mechanism, Mp is expressed as
\[M_p = C_1PL + C_2wL^2 \]
where C₁ and C₂ are constants.


The value of (C₁/C₂) is ______ (in integer).
questions.explanation:
Structural Analysis | Plastic Analysis of Frames

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Rigid-jointed portal frame with equal beam and column lengths: \(L\)
    • Left support: Fixed; Right support: Roller (horizontal plane)
    • Loads: Lateral point load \(P\) at beam level, UDL \(w\) on the beam
    • Plastic moment capacity: \(M_p\) for all sections
    • Collapse equation form: \(M_p = C_1 PL + C_2 wL^2\)
  • Aim: Find the integer value of the ratio \(C_1/C_2\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Kinematic Theorem (Upper Bound): A structure collapses when a mechanism is found for which external work equals internal work: \(W_e = W_i\).
  • Combined Mechanism: Involves both lateral sway and beam bending simultaneously, with plastic hinges at the fixed support, beam midspan, and rigid joint.
  • External Work (\(W_e\)): Sum of work done by lateral force \(P\) (through sway) and UDL \(w\) (through beam deflection profile).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Define kinematic displacements using sway angle \(\theta\).
  2. Calculate external work \(W_e\).
  3. Calculate internal work \(W_i\) for the combined mechanism.
  4. Equate \(W_e = W_i\), rearrange to the standard form, and find \(C_1/C_2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. External Work (\(W_e\)):
    Lateral displacement of beam \(= L\theta\); midspan deflection \(= \dfrac{L}{2}\theta\).
    • Work by \(P\): \(W_e(P) = P \cdot L\theta\)
    • Work by UDL \(w\) (triangular displacement profile):\[W_e(w) = w \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times L \times \dfrac{L}{2}\theta = \dfrac{1}{4}wL^2\theta \]
    • Total: \(W_e = PL\theta + 0.25\,wL^2\theta\)
  2. Internal Work (\(W_i\)) — Combined Mechanism:
    • Hinge at fixed base A: rotation \(= \theta \Rightarrow M_p\theta\)
    • Hinge at beam midspan E: relative rotation \(= 2\theta \Rightarrow 2M_p\theta\)
    • Hinge at rigid joint C: relative rotation \(= 2\theta \Rightarrow 2M_p\theta\)
    \[W_i = M_p\theta + 2M_p\theta + 2M_p\theta = 5M_p\theta \]
  3. Equating and Extracting Coefficients:\[5M_p\theta = PL\theta + 0.25\,wL^2\theta \]Dividing by \(5\theta\):\[M_p = \dfrac{1}{5}PL + \dfrac{0.25}{5}wL^2 = 0.2\,PL + 0.05\,wL^2 \]Comparing with \(M_p = C_1 PL + C_2 wL^2\):\[C_1 = 0.2, \quad C_2 = 0.05 \]
  4. Ratio:\[\dfrac{C_1}{C_2} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.05} = 4 \]Self-check: Even if internal work changes (e.g., roller gives \(3M_p\theta\)), the ratio \(C_1/C_2\) from external work geometry is always \(\dfrac{1/3}{0.25/3} = 4\). The external work geometry dictates the ratio perfectly.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4 | Accepted key range: 4 to 4

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Structural Analysis & Mechanics
questions.question:
Linearly elastic, homogeneous, uniform bars BCD and FG shown in the figure have fixed supports at B and G, respectively. For both the bars, axial rigidity is 20000 kN. A gap of 2 mm exists between D and F prior to application of any load (i.e. P = 0). Small deformation and infinitesimal strain assumptions are valid for the given bars.


(Figure not to scale)
The magnitude of the horizontal reaction (in kN) at B after application of the axial force P of 20 kN at C is ______ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Solid Mechanics | Statically Indeterminate Axial Members

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Axial rigidity: \(AE = 20{,}000\text{ kN}\) for both bars
    • Lengths: \(L_{BC} = 5\text{ m}\), \(L_{CD} = 5\text{ m}\), \(L_{FG} = 5\text{ m}\)
    • Initial gap between D and F: \(\Delta_{gap} = 2\text{ mm} = 0.002\text{ m}\)
    • Applied axial force at C: \(P = 20\text{ kN}\) (rightward)
  • Aim: Determine the magnitude of the horizontal reaction at B (\(R_B\)) in kN.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Compatibility — Gap Problem: If the free displacement of D exceeds the gap, the gap closes and bar FG provides a reaction.
  • Axial Deformation: \(\delta = \dfrac{NL}{AE}\)
  • Compatibility Equation (gap closed): \(\delta_D = \Delta_{gap} + \delta_F\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Check whether the gap closes (free expansion check).
  2. Set up internal forces in BC, CD, and FG in terms of \(R_B\).
  3. Apply compatibility to solve for \(R_B\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Free Expansion Check (no contact):
    \(N_{BC} = 20\text{ kN}\) (Tension), \(N_{CD} = 0\).\[\delta_D = \dfrac{20 \times 5}{20{,}000} = 0.005\text{ m} = 5\text{ mm} > 2\text{ mm (gap)} \]Gap closes — bar FG is engaged.
  2. Internal Forces under Contact:
    Let \(R_B\) = leftward reaction at B, \(R_G\) = leftward reaction at G.
    Global equilibrium: \(R_B + R_G = 20\text{ kN} \Rightarrow R_G = 20 - R_B\).
    • Segment BC: \(N_{BC} = +R_B\) (Tension)
    • Segment CD: \(N_{CD} = R_B - 20\) (Compression)
    • Segment FG: \(N_{FG} = -(20 - R_B) = R_B - 20\) (Compression)
  3. Displacement of D (rightward positive):\[\delta_D = \dfrac{R_B \times 5}{20{,}000} + \dfrac{(R_B-20) \times 5}{20{,}000} = \dfrac{10R_B - 100}{20{,}000} \]
  4. Displacement of F (rightward due to compression):\[\delta_F = \dfrac{(20 - R_B) \times 5}{20{,}000} = \dfrac{100 - 5R_B}{20{,}000} \]
  5. Compatibility Equation:\[\delta_D = \Delta_{gap} + \delta_F \]\[\dfrac{10R_B - 100}{20{,}000} = 0.002 + \dfrac{100 - 5R_B}{20{,}000} \]Multiply by \(20{,}000\):\[10R_B - 100 = 40 + 100 - 5R_B \]\[15R_B = 240 \implies R_B = 16\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 16 kN | Accepted key range: 16 to 16

questions.question:
A simply-supported rectangular reinforced concrete beam has a width 250 mm and an overall depth 600 mm. The effective span of the beam is 6.23 m. The beam carries a live load of 5 kN/m and super imposed dead load of 5 kN/m, in addition to its own weight. The unit weight of reinforced concrete is 25 kN/m³. Consider the load factor of 1.5 for all stated loads.
The design bending moment (in kN-m) for the limit state of collapse is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Reinforced Concrete Design | Limit State of Collapse (Flexure)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Beam type: Simply-supported, rectangular
    • Width (\(b\)) \(= 250\text{ mm}\), Overall Depth (\(D\)) \(= 600\text{ mm}\)
    • Effective span (\(L_{eff}\)) \(= 6.23\text{ m}\)
    • Live Load (LL) \(= 5\text{ kN/m}\), Superimposed Dead Load (SIDL) \(= 5\text{ kN/m}\)
    • Unit weight of concrete (\(\gamma_c\)) \(= 25\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Load factor \(= 1.5\)
  • Aim: Calculate the design bending moment (\(M_u\)) in kN·m (to 2 decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Self-Weight: \(w_{self} = b \times D \times \gamma_c\)
  • IS 456:2000 Load Combination (Clause 36.4, Table 18): \(w_u = 1.5 \times (DL + LL)\)
  • Maximum BM (simply supported, UDL): \(M_u = \dfrac{w_u L_{eff}^2}{8}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate beam self-weight per meter.
  2. Sum all un-factored loads.
  3. Apply load factor to get \(w_u\).
  4. Compute \(M_u\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Self-Weight:\[SW = 0.25 \times 0.6 \times 25 = 3.75\text{ kN/m} \]
  2. Total Un-factored Load:\[DL = 3.75 + 5.00 = 8.75\text{ kN/m} \]\[w = DL + LL = 8.75 + 5.00 = 13.75\text{ kN/m} \]
  3. Factored Design Load:\[w_u = 1.5 \times 13.75 = 20.625\text{ kN/m} \]
  4. Design Bending Moment:\[M_u = \dfrac{w_u \times L_{eff}^2}{8} = \dfrac{20.625 \times (6.23)^2}{8} \]\[M_u = \dfrac{20.625 \times 38.8129}{8} = \dfrac{800.516}{8} = 100.06\text{ kN·m} \]

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Width (in m) of a rectangular channel required to carry a discharge of 96 m³/s at a critical depth of 9.8 m is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
Use acceleration due to gravity = 9.8 m/s²
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow (Critical Flow)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel shape: Rectangular
    • Total discharge (\(Q\)) \(= 96\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Critical depth (\(y_c\)) \(= 9.8\text{ m}\)
    • Acceleration due to gravity (\(g\)) \(= 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Find the required channel width (\(B\)) in meters (rounded to two decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Critical Flow in Rectangular Channels: At critical conditions (Froude number \(F_r = 1\)):\[y_c = \left(\dfrac{q^2}{g}\right)^{1/3} \]where \(q = Q/B\) is the discharge per unit width.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Rearrange the critical depth formula to solve for \(q\).
  2. Substitute known values to compute \(q\).
  3. Use \(q = Q/B\) to solve for \(B\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Solve for \(q\):\[y_c^3 = \dfrac{q^2}{g} \implies q^2 = y_c^3 \times g \]Substituting \(y_c = 9.8\text{ m}\) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\):\[q^2 = (9.8)^3 \times 9.8 = (9.8)^4 \]\[q = (9.8)^2 = 96.04\text{ m}^2/\text{s} \]
  2. Solve for Channel Width (\(B\)):\[B = \dfrac{Q}{q} = \dfrac{96}{96.04} = 0.9996\text{ m} \approx 1.00\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.00 m | Accepted key range: 0.90 to 1.10

questions.question:
The cross section of a 0.5 m wide vertical gate holding water and oil is shown in the figure. The unit weights of water and oil are 10 kN/m³ and 7.5 kN/m³, respectively.


(Figure not to scale)
The horizontal hydrostatic force (in kN) acting on the vertical gate is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Hydrostatic Forces

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Width of vertical gate, \(B = 0.5\text{ m}\)
    • Depth of oil layer, \(h_{\text{oil}} = 0.5\text{ m}\); Unit weight of oil, \(\gamma_{\text{oil}} = 7.5\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Depth of water layer, \(h_{\text{water}} = 1.0\text{ m}\); Unit weight of water, \(\gamma_{\text{water}} = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total horizontal hydrostatic force (kN) acting on the vertical gate.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Hydrostatic pressure variation: \(P = \int \gamma\,dz\)
  • For multi-layered fluids, pressure at an interface transfers down and adds to the underlying fluid's pressure.
  • Total hydrostatic force = Area of pressure diagram \(\times\) Width of gate.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Compute pressure intensities at the free surface, oil-water interface, and gate bottom.
  2. Calculate force on oil portion (triangular pressure diagram).
  3. Calculate force on water portion (trapezoidal pressure diagram).
  4. Sum individual forces.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Pressure Computations:
    • At free surface: \(P_0 = 0\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • At oil-water interface: \(P_1 = 7.5 \times 0.5 = 3.75\text{ kN/m}^2\)
    • At gate bottom: \(P_2 = 3.75 + (10 \times 1.0) = 13.75\text{ kN/m}^2\)
  2. Force on oil portion (triangle):\[F_{\text{oil}} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times P_1 \times h_{\text{oil}} \times B = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3.75 \times 0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.469\text{ kN} \]
  3. Force on water portion (trapezoid):\[F_{\text{water}} = \dfrac{P_1 + P_2}{2} \times h_{\text{water}} \times B = \dfrac{3.75 + 13.75}{2} \times 1.0 \times 0.5 = 8.75 \times 0.5 = 4.375\text{ kN} \]
  4. Total Force:\[F = F_{\text{oil}} + F_{\text{water}} = 0.469 + 4.375 = 4.844\text{ kN} \approx 4.84\text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 4.84 kN | Accepted key range: 4.75 to 5.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A centrifugal pump is delivering water from an underground tank to an overhead reservoir against a static head of 35 m through a 2 km long, 250 mm diameter pipe. The head-discharge characteristic of the pump is given by
\[H = 140 - 9000Q^2 \]
where H is the head (in m) generated by the pump and Q is the discharge (in m³/s) of the pump.
Neglecting all minor losses, the head (in m) generated by the pump is ______ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
Use: Darcy-Weisbach friction factor f = 0.04
Acceleration due to gravity = 9.81 m/s²
\( \pi = 3.14 \)
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Pipe Flow & Pumps

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Static head: \(H_{\text{stat}} = 35\text{ m}\)
    • Pipe length: \(L = 2000\text{ m}\), Diameter: \(D = 0.25\text{ m}\)
    • Pump characteristic: \(H = 140 - 9000Q^2\)
    • Friction factor: \(f = 0.04\), \(g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2\), \(\pi = 3.14\)
    • Minor losses neglected.
  • Aim: Determine the head generated by the pump (\(H\) in m), rounded to nearest integer.

3. Core Concepts:

  • System Head: \(H_{\text{sys}} = H_{\text{stat}} + h_f\)
  • Darcy-Weisbach: \(h_f = \dfrac{8fLQ^2}{\pi^2 g D^5}\)
  • Operating Point: \(H_{\text{pump}} = H_{\text{sys}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Express \(h_f\) as a function of \(Q^2\).
  2. Write the system head equation.
  3. Equate to pump characteristic and solve for \(Q^2\).
  4. Substitute \(Q^2\) back into pump equation to find \(H\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Friction Head Loss Coefficient:\[h_f = \dfrac{8 \times 0.04 \times 2000}{(3.14)^2 \times 9.81 \times (0.25)^5} \times Q^2 = \dfrac{640}{0.09446} Q^2 \approx 6775.66\,Q^2 \]
  2. System Head:\[H_{\text{sys}} = 35 + 6775.66\,Q^2 \]
  3. Operating Point:\[140 - 9000Q^2 = 35 + 6775.66Q^2 \]\[105 = 15775.66\,Q^2 \implies Q^2 = \dfrac{105}{15775.66} \approx 0.006656\text{ m}^6/\text{s}^2 \]
  4. Head Generated:\[H = 140 - 9000 \times 0.006656 = 140 - 59.90 = 80.10\text{ m} \approx 80\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 80 m | Accepted key range: 78 to 82

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q55

questions.question:
The flow depth for a discharge of 10 m³/s in a wide rectangular channel is 2.0 m. Assume that the flow is uniform.
If the discharge is doubled, the flow depth (in m) in this channel is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Open Channel Flow | Uniform Flow

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel type: Wide rectangular
    • Initial: \(Q_1 = 10\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\), \(y_1 = 2.0\text{ m}\)
    • Final: \(Q_2 = 20\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\) (doubled)
    • Flow is uniform; \(S\), \(B\), \(n\) are constant.
  • Aim: Calculate the new uniform flow depth \(y_2\) in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • For a wide rectangular channel: hydraulic radius \(R \approx y\).
  • Manning's Equation: \(Q = \dfrac{B}{n} y^{5/3} \sqrt{S}\)
  • Since \(B\), \(n\), and \(S\) are constant: \(Q \propto y^{5/3}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Set up ratio using Manning's proportionality.
  2. Substitute knowns and solve for \(y_2\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Ratio Setup:\[\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_1} = \left(\dfrac{y_2}{y_1}\right)^{5/3} \implies \dfrac{20}{10} = \left(\dfrac{y_2}{2.0}\right)^{5/3} \]
  2. Solve for \(y_2\):\[2 = \left(\dfrac{y_2}{2.0}\right)^{5/3} \]Taking power \(3/5\) on both sides:\[\dfrac{y_2}{2.0} = 2^{3/5} = 2^{0.6} \approx 1.5157 \]\[y_2 = 2.0 \times 1.5157 = 3.031\text{ m} \approx 3.03\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3.03 m | Accepted key range: 3.00 to 3.20

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
For a clayey soil stratum, the time required for degree of consolidation from 25 % to 50 % is 30 days.
The total time (in days) required for 90 % degree of consolidation of the same soil stratum is ______ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Time for consolidation from 25% to 50%: \(\Delta t = 30\text{ days}\)
    • Soil properties \(c_v\) and \(H\) are constant.
  • Aim: Determine the total time to reach 90% consolidation (\(t_{90}\)) in days.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Time Factor: \(T_v = \dfrac{c_v t}{H^2} \implies t \propto T_v\)
  • For \(U \le 60\%\): \(T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{4} U^2\)  (\(U\) in decimals)
  • For \(U > 60\%\): \(T_v = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - U\%)\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate \(T_v\) for \(U = 25\%\) and \(U = 50\%\).
  2. Deduce the constant \(c_v/H^2\) using \(\Delta t = 30\) days.
  3. Calculate \(T_v\) for \(U = 90\%\).
  4. Compute the total time \(t_{90}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Time Factors for 25% and 50%:\[T_{v,25} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.25)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{64} \approx 0.04909 \]\[T_{v,50} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(0.50)^2 = \dfrac{\pi}{16} \approx 0.19635 \]\[\Delta T_v = \dfrac{\pi}{16} - \dfrac{\pi}{64} = \dfrac{3\pi}{64} \approx 0.14726 \]
  2. Deduce Constant \(c_v/H^2\):\[\dfrac{c_v}{H^2} = \dfrac{\Delta T_v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{3\pi/64}{30} = \dfrac{\pi}{640}\text{ days}^{-1} \]
  3. Time Factor for 90%:\[T_{v,90} = 1.781 - 0.933\log_{10}(100 - 90) = 1.781 - 0.933(1) = 0.848 \]
  4. Total Time:\[t_{90} = \dfrac{T_{v,90}}{c_v/H^2} = \dfrac{0.848}{\pi/640} = \dfrac{0.848 \times 640}{\pi} = \dfrac{542.72}{3.14159} \approx 172.75\text{ days} \approx 173\text{ days} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 173 days | Accepted key range: 170 to 174

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q57

questions.question:
The ultimate bearing capacity of a 1 m wide strip footing is 532.80 kPa, when it is embedded at 1 m depth in dry cohesionless soil. The soil has a unit weight of 18 kN/m³. The ultimate bearing capacity is 864 kPa when the depth of embedment becomes 2 m.
Neglecting the effect of the depth factor, the bearing capacity factor Nq is ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Shallow Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Strip footing width: \(B = 1\text{ m}\); Dry cohesionless soil: \(c = 0\)
    • Unit weight: \(\gamma = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Case 1: \(D_{f1} = 1\text{ m}\), \(q_{u1} = 532.80\text{ kPa}\)
    • Case 2: \(D_{f2} = 2\text{ m}\), \(q_{u2} = 864\text{ kPa}\)
    • Depth factors neglected.
  • Aim: Calculate the bearing capacity factor \(N_q\).

3. Core Concepts:

Terzaghi's Bearing Capacity for strip footing on cohesionless soil (\(c = 0\)):\[q_u = \gamma D_f N_q + 0.5\,\gamma B N_\gamma \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Formulate two equations for the two depth cases.
  2. Subtract to eliminate \(N_\gamma\) and isolate \(N_q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Case 1 (\(D_f = 1\text{ m}\)):\[532.80 = 18(1)N_q + 0.5(18)(1)N_\gamma = 18N_q + 9N_\gamma \quad \cdots (1) \]
  2. Case 2 (\(D_f = 2\text{ m}\)):\[864 = 18(2)N_q + 0.5(18)(1)N_\gamma = 36N_q + 9N_\gamma \quad \cdots (2) \]
  3. Subtract Eq. (1) from Eq. (2):\[864 - 532.80 = 18N_q \]\[331.20 = 18N_q \implies N_q = \dfrac{331.20}{18} = 18.4 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(N_q = 18.4\) | Accepted key range: 18.2 to 18.6

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A building is proposed in an area having thick deposit of silty clay. The water table is at the ground surface. The saturated unit weight of soil is 18 kN/m³ and unit weight of water is 10 kN/m³. The maximum vertical load (P) on a column of the proposed building is 2000 kN.
Consider \( \sigma_z \le 0.1 \sigma'_v \) for computation of the minimum depth of soil exploration.
\( \sigma'_v \) is the effective vertical overburden stress. \( \sigma_z \) is the increase in the vertical stress at depth Z below load P as per the Boussinesq's stress theory.
Based on above, the minimum depth (in m) of soil exploration required for the foundation design is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Exploration & Stresses

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Saturated unit weight: \(\gamma_{\text{sat}} = 18\text{ kN/m}^3\)
    • Unit weight of water: \(\gamma_w = 10\text{ kN/m}^3\) (water table at ground level)
    • Point vertical load: \(P = 2000\text{ kN}\)
    • Condition: \(\sigma_z \le 0.1\,\sigma'_v\)
  • Aim: Evaluate the minimum soil exploration depth \(z\) in meters directly beneath the column.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Effective vertical stress: \(\sigma'_v = \gamma' \cdot z = (\gamma_{\text{sat}} - \gamma_w) \cdot z\)
  • Boussinesq's vertical stress (directly below load, \(r = 0\)):\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3P}{2\pi z^2} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine effective unit weight \(\gamma'\).
  2. Write expressions for \(\sigma'_v\) and \(\sigma_z\) in terms of \(z\).
  3. Equate \(\sigma_z = 0.1\,\sigma'_v\) and solve for \(z\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Stresses:\[\gamma' = 18 - 10 = 8\text{ kN/m}^3 \]\[\sigma'_v = 8z \quad (\text{kN/m}^2) \]\[\sigma_z = \dfrac{3 \times 2000}{2\pi z^2} = \dfrac{3000}{\pi z^2} \quad (\text{kN/m}^2) \]
  2. Apply Threshold Condition:\[\dfrac{3000}{\pi z^2} = 0.1 \times 8z = 0.8z \]\[z^3 = \dfrac{3000}{0.8\pi} = \dfrac{3750}{\pi} = 1193.66 \]\[ z = \sqrt[3]{1193.66} \approx 10.61\text{ m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10.61 m | Accepted key range: 10.00 to 11.20

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
For a given traffic stream, the speed-density relationship is given as:
\[v = v_o \ln \left( \dfrac{k_j}{k} \right) \]
where \( v \) is the mean speed (in km/h), and \( k \) is the density (in veh/km).
Considering \( v_o \) as 45 km/h, and \( k_j \) as 200 veh/km, the maximum flow (in veh/h) for the given stream is _________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Speed-density relationship (Greenberg's model): \(v = v_o \ln\left(\dfrac{k_j}{k}\right)\)
    • Free flow speed: \(v_o = 45\text{ km/h}\)
    • Jam density: \(k_j = 200\text{ veh/km}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the maximum flow (\(q_{max}\)) in veh/h, rounded to nearest integer.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Fundamental Traffic Equation: \(q = k \cdot v\)
  • Maximum Flow Condition: \(\dfrac{dq}{dk} = 0\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute speed-density relation into \(q = k \cdot v\).
  2. Differentiate \(q\) w.r.t. \(k\) and set to zero to find \(k_m\).
  3. Substitute \(k_m\) back to get \(q_{max}\).
  4. Compute numerically.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Flow equation:\[q = k \cdot v_o \ln\left(\dfrac{k_j}{k}\right) \]
  2. Differentiate and set to zero:\[\dfrac{dq}{dk} = v_o \ln\left(\dfrac{k_j}{k}\right) - v_o = 0 \implies \ln\left(\dfrac{k_j}{k}\right) = 1 \implies k_m = \dfrac{k_j}{e} \](Standard result: density at capacity = jam density / Euler's number)
  3. Maximum flow:\[q_{max} = \dfrac{k_j}{e} \cdot v_o \ln(e) = \dfrac{v_o \cdot k_j}{e} \]
  4. Numerical computation:\[q_{max} = \dfrac{45 \times 200}{2.71828} = \dfrac{9000}{2.71828} \approx 3311\text{ veh/h} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3311 veh/h | Accepted key range: 3300 to 3350

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
A vertical curve is formed by a descending gradient of 1 in 40 meeting an ascending gradient of 1 in 50. Consider the following:
Stopping Sight Distance (SSD) = 90 m
Height of headlight of a vehicle above the road surface = 0.75 m
Headlight beam angle with respect to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle = 1.2°
Based on the sight distance criteria, the design length (in m) of the vertical curve is _________ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Highway Geometric Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Descending gradient: \(n_1 = 1\text{ in }40 = -0.025\)
    • Ascending gradient: \(n_2 = 1\text{ in }50 = +0.020\)
    • Stopping Sight Distance: \(S = 90\text{ m}\)
    • Height of headlight: \(h_1 = 0.75\text{ m}\)
    • Headlight beam angle: \(\alpha = 1.2^\circ\)
  • Aim: Determine the design length of the valley (sag) vertical curve (\(L\)) in meters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Deviation Angle: \(N = |n_2 - n_1|\)
  • Valley Curve Length Formulas (IRC:73):
    • If \(L > S\): \(\quad L = \dfrac{NS^2}{2(h_1 + S\tan\alpha)}\)
    • If \(L < S\): \(\quad L = 2S - \dfrac{2(h_1 + S\tan\alpha)}{N}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate deviation angle \(N\).
  2. Compute beam spread term \(2(h_1 + S\tan\alpha)\).
  3. Assume \(L > S\) and check validity; if invalid, use \(L < S\) formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Deviation Angle:\[N = |-0.025 - (+0.020)| = 0.045 \]
  2. Beam Spread Term:\[2(0.75 + 90 \times \tan 1.2^\circ) = 2(0.75 + 90 \times 0.020953) = 2(0.75 + 1.8857) = 2(2.6357) = 5.271\text{ m} \]
  3. Assume \(L > S\):\[L = \dfrac{0.045 \times 90^2}{5.271} = \dfrac{364.5}{5.271} = 69.14\text{ m} \]Check: \(69.14\text{ m} \not> 90\text{ m}\) → assumption invalid.
  4. Use \(L < S\) formula:\[L = 2(90) - \dfrac{5.271}{0.045} = 180 - 117.14 = 62.86\text{ m} \approx 63\text{ m} \]Check: \(62.86\text{ m} < 90\text{ m}\) ✓

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 63 m | Accepted key range: 60 to 67

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Surveying & Geomatics
questions.question:
Interior angles measured at the locations of a closed traverse ABCDA are given in table below.

LocationInterior angle
A71° 1' 40''
B104° 54' 23''
C107° 54' 10''
D76° 20' 42''

The total error in the measured angles (in degrees) is _____________ (rounded off to three decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Geomatics Engineering | Surveying (Traverse)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Interior angles of 4-sided closed traverse ABCDA:
    • \(A = 71^\circ 1' 40''\)
    • \(B = 104^\circ 54' 23''\)
    • \(C = 107^\circ 54' 10''\)
    • \(D = 76^\circ 20' 42''\)
  • Aim: Calculate the total angular error in decimal degrees (rounded to 3 decimal places).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Theoretical sum for \(n\)-sided polygon: \(\Sigma_{\text{theoretical}} = (2n-4) \times 90^\circ\)
  • Angular Error: \(\text{Error} = \Sigma_{\text{measured}} - \Sigma_{\text{theoretical}}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Sum the measured angles in DMS.
  2. Calculate the theoretical sum for \(n = 4\).
  3. Find the DMS error and convert to decimal degrees.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Sum of Seconds: \(40 + 23 + 10 + 42 = 115'' = 1' + 55''\)  (carry \(1'\))
  2. Sum of Minutes: \(1 + 54 + 54 + 20 + 1_{\text{carry}} = 130' = 2^\circ + 10'\)  (carry \(2^\circ\))
  3. Sum of Degrees: \(71 + 104 + 107 + 76 + 2_{\text{carry}} = 360^\circ\)
  4. Total Measured Sum: \(360^\circ 10' 55''\)
  5. Theoretical Sum (\(n=4\)):\[\Sigma_{\text{theoretical}} = (2 \times 4 - 4) \times 90^\circ = 360^\circ \]
  6. Angular Error:\[\text{Error} = 360^\circ 10' 55'' - 360^\circ 0' 0'' = 0^\circ 10' 55'' \]
  7. Convert to Decimal Degrees:\[\text{Error} = 0 + \dfrac{10}{60} + \dfrac{55}{3600} = 0.16667 + 0.01528 = 0.18194^\circ \approx 0.182^\circ \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.182° | Accepted key range: 0.180 to 0.184

questions.title: GATE CE 2026 Set 2 | CE Q63

questions.question:
The analysis of major cations and anions in a water sample collected from a city's water supply is given below. Ions present in minor concentrations are not given.

AnionsCl⁻SO₄²⁻HCO₃⁻CO₃²⁻

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • \([HCO_3^-] = 1.0\text{ mM}\), \([CO_3^{2-}] = 0.01\text{ mM}\)
    • Carbonate equilibrium: \(HCO_3^- \rightleftharpoons H^+ + CO_3^{2-}\), \(pK = 10.3\)
    • Hypochlorous acid equilibrium: \(HOCl \rightleftharpoons H^+ + OCl^-\), \(pK = 7.5\)
  • Aim: Find the percentage of \(HOCl\) in total free chlorine (\(HOCl + OCl^-\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • The coexistence of \(HCO_3^-\) and \(CO_3^{2-}\) in equilibrium establishes the \([H^+]\) (and hence pH) of the water.
  • Acid Dissociation: \(K_a = \dfrac{[H^+][A^-]}{[HA]}\)
  • Free Chlorine fraction: \(\%HOCl = \dfrac{[HOCl]}{[HOCl]+[OCl^-]} \times 100\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Use carbonate equilibrium to find \([H^+]\).
  2. Use \([H^+]\) in the hypochlorous acid equilibrium to find the \([OCl^-]/[HOCl]\) ratio.
  3. Calculate the \(\%HOCl\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find \([H^+]\) from carbonate equilibrium:\[ K_a = 10^{-10.3} = \dfrac{[H^+] \times 0.01\text{ mM}}{1.0\text{ mM}} = [H^+] \times 10^{-2} \]\[ [H^+] = \dfrac{10^{-10.3}}{10^{-2}} = 10^{-8.3}\text{ M} \quad (\text{pH} = 8.3) \]
  2. Find \([OCl^-]/[HOCl]\) ratio:\[ K_{HOCl} = 10^{-7.5} = 10^{-8.3} \times \dfrac{[OCl^-]}{[HOCl]} \]\[ \dfrac{[OCl^-]}{[HOCl]} = \dfrac{10^{-7.5}}{10^{-8.3}} = 10^{0.8} = 6.310 \]
  3. Percentage of \(HOCl\):\[\%HOCl = \dfrac{1}{1 + 6.310} \times 100 = \dfrac{1}{7.310} \times 100 \approx 13.68\% \approx 14\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14% | Accepted key range: 13 to 15

questions.question:
Anaerobic bacteria are being utilized for the destruction of biodegradable organic content of wastewater measured in terms of Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD). The yield coefficient (Y) is 0.06 gram Volatile Suspended Solids (VSS) per gram of COD. Bacterial biomass forms the sludge during the process. The proximate chemical formula of anaerobic bacteria is C₆H₇NO₂.
The COD (in %) converted into bacterial biomass is _____ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Biomass Yield: \(Y = 0.06\text{ g VSS}/\text{g COD}\) consumed
    • Biomass formula: \(C_6H_7NO_2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the percentage of consumed COD converted into bacterial biomass.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Biomass COD Equivalent: Oxygen required to fully oxidize 1 g of VSS.
  • COD of Biomass: Found by balancing the oxidation reaction of \(C_6H_7NO_2\) (nitrogen converts to \(NH_3\)).
  • Mass Balance: COD consumed = COD for energy + COD trapped in biomass.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate molar mass of \(C_6H_7NO_2\).
  2. Balance the oxidation equation to find moles of \(O_2\) per mole of biomass.
  3. Calculate oxygen equivalent (g COD / g VSS).
  4. Multiply by yield \(Y\) to get fraction of COD in biomass; convert to percentage.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Molar Mass of \(C_6H_7NO_2\):\[\text{MW} = (6 \times 12) + (7 \times 1) + (1 \times 14) + (2 \times 16) = 72 + 7 + 14 + 32 = 125\text{ g/mol} \]
  2. Balanced Oxidation Equation:
    Moles of \(O_2\) required \(= c + \dfrac{h - 3n}{4} - \dfrac{o}{2}\)  (with \(c=6, h=7, o=2, n=1\)):\[= 6 + \dfrac{7-3}{4} - \dfrac{2}{2} = 6 + 1 - 1 = 6\text{ moles} \]\[C_6H_7NO_2 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + NH_3 + 2H_2O \]
  3. Oxygen Equivalent:\[\dfrac{6 \times 32\text{ g }O_2}{125\text{ g VSS}} = \dfrac{192}{125} = 1.536\text{ g COD/g VSS} \]
  4. Fraction of COD converted to biomass:\[0.06\text{ g VSS} \times 1.536\text{ g COD/g VSS} = 0.09216\text{ g COD} \]\[\% = 0.09216 \times 100 = 9.216\% \approx 9\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 9% | Accepted key range: 8 to 10

questions.question:
In an industry, a cyclone collector with 80 % efficiency is installed for air purification, followed by an electrostatic precipitator with 50 % efficiency. The concentration of particles entering the cyclone collector is 10 mg/m³.
The concentration (in mg/m³) of particles exiting the precipitator is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Cyclone collector efficiency: \(\eta_1 = 80\% = 0.80\)
    • Electrostatic precipitator (ESP) efficiency: \(\eta_2 = 50\% = 0.50\)
    • Input particulate concentration: \(C_{in} = 10\text{ mg/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the exit concentration after both devices in series (mg/m³), rounded to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

Removal Efficiency in Series: The outlet of the first device is the inlet of the second.\[C_{out} = C_{in} \times (1 - \eta_1) \times (1 - \eta_2) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate concentration after the cyclone collector.
  2. Use that as input to the ESP and calculate the final exit concentration.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. After Cyclone Collector:\[C_1 = 10 \times (1 - 0.80) = 10 \times 0.20 = 2.0\text{ mg/m}^3 \]
  2. After ESP (Final Exit):\[C_{out} = 2.0 \times (1 - 0.50) = 2.0 \times 0.50 = 1.00\text{ mg/m}^3 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 1.00 mg/m³ | Accepted key range: 0.90 to 1.10
